Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

topsy-turvy adjective

also upside down (in disorder), everything was upside down, everything was topsy-turvy, in a mess

classical

Sall. Cat. 10.1: saevīre fortūna ac miscēre omnia coepit (Lewis & Short s.v. saeviō)

omnia miscēre

turn everything upside down, throw everything into confusion

Miscēre, to mix, is also to throw into disorder; in the passive, omnia mixta.

Other words

  • sūrsum deorsum — topsy-turvy, upside down (in disorder)

    two adverbs, “upwards, downwards” · also used · modern · Traupman 110: omnia erant sūrsum deorsum

    Classically the pair means “up and down, to and fro”, of movement (see up and down). Lewis & Short gives no instance of it for things in disorder, Traupman’s sense; there omnia is the subject: “everything was up and down”.

See also flip over, up and down.
